quotes.text: The Savior Jesus Christ perfectly exemplified this principle. Throughout His ministry, He truly saw the people around Him. He saw the woman at the well, the leper, the blind man, and the child. Where others saw labels, He saw beloved sons and daughters of God. Even of the rich young man who later walked away from Him sorrowing, the scriptures say, â[And] Jesus beholding him loved him.â

quotes.text: The good Samaritan also chose to see. Rather than allowing labels or differences to distract him, he saw a child of God in need and acted. quotes.text: Seeing others as children of God also influences the way we see ourselves, yet the world encourages us to see ourselves and others differently. The world invites us to focus on labels rather than eternal identity.

quotes.text: Like many people, I have sometimes viewed myself through the lens of such labels. When President Oaks extended my new calling, he told me, âYouâve been called for who you are. quotes.text: My dear friends, I leave you a final sawubona. I see you. More important, your Heavenly Father sees you. Your Savior, Jesus Christ, sees you. They know your name, your circumstances, your gifts, and your divine potential.
